children: Prediction markets have shown little movement after President Donald Trump floated a $5,000 "Trump dividend" for every adult U.S. citizen if Republicans keep both the House and Senate in November’s midterm elections.

Traders on Kalshi continue to assign just a 15% probability that the GOP retains unified control of Congress. That figure has not risen in recent weeks. In early May, the same market priced a Republican sweep of both chambers at 26.9%. The odds have declined steadily since then.

By contrast, Kalshi currently gives Democrats a 46.5% chance of winning both the House and Senate. A split outcome—Democratic House and Republican Senate—stands at 36%. The inverse split, a Republican House and Democratic Senate, is priced at only 1.5%.

Trump presented the cash payment as a reward for voters if his party holds both chambers, likening it to a corporate distribution to shareholders and tying it to what he called the nation’s economic success. The proposal would require congressional approval and would carry a multi-trillion-dollar price tag.
Markets, however, have not treated the pledge as a material shift in the midterm outlook. The implied probabilities remain consistent with the downward trend that has been in place for months.

title: Markets shrug off Trump’s $5,000 midterm ‘dividend’
